items.title: Call to Order
notes: Mayor Watters welcomed everyone and called the meeting to order.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Lustgarten-Evoy read the Land Acknowledgement.

items.title: Addendums and Corrections to the Agenda
notes: There were no addendums or corrections to the agenda.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest Under the Municipal Conflict of Interest
notes: Act
None declared.

items.title: Introduction of Local Artist - Millie Cumming
notes: Barb Lee, Elora Arts Council introduced Millie Cumming as the local artist currently displaying her art in the Council Chamber. She noted a new display at the Sportsplex showcasing the work of Centre Wellington High School students.
M. Cumming shared her love for textile art and explained her work is inspired by nature, cottaging, peace and renewal.

items.title: Fergus Scottish Festival
notes: Matthew Bennett-Monty, President of the Board of Directors provided an overview of the 2023 festival and highlights, including the heavy events, featured guests from Outlander, the Whisky Village, the parade, the economic and tourism impact, and the wonderful and dedicated volunteers.

items.title: Dr. Sarah Gower & Alison Armstrong, Wellington Health Care Alliance
notes: re: Physician Retention & Recruitment

Dr. Gower provided an overview of the ongoing recruitment and retention initiatives. She noted the successful recruitment efforts to bring new family physicians and obstetric specialists, and how helpful having access to temporary housing has been.

items.title: Pierre Chauvin, MHBC re RZ13/22 - 223 St. Andrew Street, E., Fergus
notes: outlined the scope of the proposed development, including 17 residential units and 2 commercial units, 4 barrier free units and 13 parking spaces.

He outlined the changes from the original concept plan and the redesign, including coloured stone to match the surrounding buildings, larger ground floor windows and mouldings, accentuation of the corners and entablature at the top of the 1st, 4th and 5th storeys. He noted the proposed development will bring much needed rental housing to the community.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Mayor Watters noted Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. Any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate discussion and/or action.

items.title: Changes to Open-Air Burning By-Law
notes: Report from T. Mulvey, Fire Chief

T. Mulvey, Fire Chief provided an overview of the report, indicating Fire Services is proposing amendments to the open-air burn by-law as a housekeeping measure. The amendments include the addition of Class D permits and improved wording to clarify permitted locations for Class A permits.

items.title: RFP#59-23 Fire Pumper Truck
notes: Report from S. Lloyd-Smith, Manager of Purchasing and Risk Management

A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report and Fire Chief Mulvey responded to questions regarding the challenges with procurement of the new pumper truck and consideration for the disposition of the old truck.

items.title: Community Improvement Plan 2024 Implementation Report
notes: Report from S. Litchfield, Economic Development Coordinator S. Litchfield, Economic Development Coordinator provided an overview of the report, indicating Council adopted the updated Community Improvement Plan, including an implementation process. She noted this report addresses the roles and responsibilities and delivery details for the program.

items.title: Heritage Permit Application (HP2024-01) - 27-43 West Mill Street, Elora
notes: Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services provided an overview of the report, noting the current heritage permit application is for the addition of a balcony on the second storey of the front façade facing West Mill Street, reinstating historic balconies that once existed at the property but have been removed. She indicated Heritage Centre Wellington is supportive of the application with conditions as recommended by the heritage consultant in the Heritage Impact Assessment.

M. Iglesias and C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services responded to questions regarding AODA compliance, removal of the non-support columns to aid in snow removal, conditions of the encroachment agreement, access to the underground utilities, and provided clarification regarding the desire to support restoring heritage buildings to their original state.

items.title: Encroachment Agreement between the Township of Centre Wellington
notes: and Kat Florence Canada Company Limited for a Proposed Balcony over the Municipal Sidewalk at 43 West Mill Street in Elora Report from C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services provided an overview of the report and outlined the number of conditions proposed such as lighting, inspections, insurance and indemnification.

items.title: Decision Report RZ013/22 - 223 St. Andrew St. E., Fergus
notes: Report M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services provided an overview of the report, noting the property is located on the north side of St. Andrew Street E., just east of Gowrie Street N., in the downtown core of the Fergus Urban Centre. She indicated the applicant is seeking a zoning amendment to allow an increased height of 16.7m to facilitate construction of a 5-storey mixed use building with 163m2 (approx.
1,800ft2) commercial use at the ground floor in 2 separate units and 17 residential units above with an elevator.
M. Iglesias responded to questions regarding the number of units on the 5th storey and provided clarification regarding the reduction in parking requirements.
Mayor Watters called for a 10 minute recess.
After reflection, Councillor Craddock put forward the following motion to reconsider the previous decision:
Councillor Craddock apologized for abstaining from the vote as he was undecided and put forward the following motion.

items.title: Electric Vehicle (EV) ChargeON Program
notes: Report from D. Masiero, Manager of Environmental Services D. Masiero, Manager of Environmental Services provided an overview of the report indicating the Ontario Electric Vehicle (EV) ChargeON Program provides funding for the installation of public electric vehicle (EV) chargers in Ontario communities outside of major cities. The Township has applied for grant funding to allow for the installation of eight (8) charging stations in Centre Wellington.
C. Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure services responded to questions regarding ongoing operation and maintenance, future revenue source and location of the various locations.

items.title: Update on Township Water Supply Projects
notes: Report from A. Gilmore, Manager of Engineering

A. Gilmore, Manager of Engineering provided an overview of the water supply projects, including the Water Supply Master Plan (2019), Wells F2/F5 Replacement, New Well Exploration Program, Wellfield Capacity Assessment, the Permit to Take Water Renewal Application and the short term and long term next steps.
D. Wilson, CAO indicated Council has given staff direction to develop a water/wastewater service allocation policy which ties into the activity currently underway.
Staff responded to questions regarding permits for taking water, Class EA environmental study and impacts to surrounding wells, and the status of Well F5.

motions.item_title: Encroachment Agreement between the Township of Centre Wellington
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington supports the construction of a balcony on and over Township property related to the redevelopment of the former "Commercial Hotel" building located at 43 West Mill Street in Elora as outlined in Report No. IS2024-01; AND THAT Council authorizes the Managing Director of Infrastructure Services to execute an Encroachment Agreement between the Township of Centre Wellington and Kat Florence Canada Company Limited for a balcony structure within the Township's right-of-way, subject to the following conditions: 1. That the balcony is designed and constructed to cantilever over the municipal sidewalk; and 2. That an unobstructed pedestrian clear zone of 3.25 m metres from the sidewalk surface to the underside of the balcony and 2.00 metres from the facade of the building to the inside face of the vertical columns be maintained at all times; 3. That the five vertical columns connected to the sidewalk be designed and constructed in a way that they are non-structural and can be easily removed by the proponent at the Township's request to accommodate future operation and maintenance activities related to the municipal and utilities infrastructure within the right-of-way; 4. That the proponent provide adequate lighting within the pedestrian area in accordance with Township standards; 5. That appropriate insurance coverage and indemnification be obtained from the proponent in accordance with Township policy; and, 6. That the balcony be inspected by a qualified professional at a minimum frequency of once every five years, as recommended by the proponent's heritage consultant, with any recommendations or deficiencies identified in the inspection report addressed within 12 months of date of the inspection.
